newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures come back in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures come back in moderate trade.

text.p: Australian wheat futures slipped on Tuesday with weakness most notable in nearby months.

November 1997 and January 1998, the two contracts nearest deliveries of new crop wheat, were the only trades. November fell by A$2.50 a tonne to A$173.50 on four lots while market leader January edged back by 50 cents to A$173.50 on 16 lots.
Settlement prices across the range were mostly down by 50 cents, although September 1997 fell by A$8.00 a tonne.

Cash prices rose by A$1.00 a tonne to about A$169.00 for Australian Standard White Newcastle for December/January, private traders said. This put cash on a futures-eqivalent price of A$174.00, in line with January futures.
